title: A Blood Glucose Control Framework Based on Reinforcement Learning With Safety and Interpretability: In Silico Validation
domain: Type 1 diabetes; automated insulin delivery; in-silico control
dataset_or_cohort: UVA/Padova Type 1 Diabetes Simulator virtual adult and adolescent populations
sample_scale: 20 virtual subjects (10 adults and 10 adolescents), each simulated for 20 days with four or five randomized meals per day
institution_count: NA: simulator study with no clinical institution or patient recruitment
split_strategy: Online predictors use the trailing 250 minutes; prediction and control are evaluated in the same simulator subjects, with no independent subject-level or external split
observation_process: Glucose, delivered insulin, meal intake, and time information sampled every 5 minutes; the controller state includes a 60-minute history window
missingness: NA: simulator observations are generated as complete trajectories; no missing-data mechanism reported
censoring_or_competing_events: NA: no censoring, death, or competing event in the virtual-subject experiment
state: Glucose, insulin, meal, and time features plus a nine-dimensional DAN-derived contextual state
observation_decoder: Random-forest regression directly forecasts glucose; auxiliary deep architecture processes the extended state for policy learning
action: Continuous insulin delivery with safety-actor suspension/additional-insulin commands and oral-carbohydrate rescue
action_provenance: SAC-selected simulated pump commands; PID guides the initial control period and the rule-based safety actor can override unsafe commands
transition_mechanism: Online random-forest and DAN glucose predictors support imagined SAC rollouts; the random forest supplies point forecasts and DAN extends the state context
maximum_horizon: 30-minute glucose prediction, 45-minute safety look-ahead, 150-minute imagined rollout, and 20-day closed-loop evaluation
rollout_regime: Free-running imagined rollout inside the controller and closed-loop operation in the UVA/Padova simulator.
capability_claim: Planning — sequential insulin control optimized through model rollouts with an explicit safety layer.
baselines: PID controller and algorithm/component comparisons reported in the article
state_fidelity_metrics: Thirty-minute glucose MAE plus TIR, TBR, TAR, median glucose, and CVGA control zones
transition_metrics: Thirty-minute MAE: adolescents 28.1±19.1 mg/dL (DAN) and 13.3±13.9 (RFR); adults 21.8±15.4 and 12.4±11.7; no error-versus-horizon curve
rollout_stability: Twenty-day closed-loop trajectories remain controlled, but error or control performance is not resolved across rollout horizons
action_sensitivity: No structured action-removal or dose-perturbation study; PID comparison does not isolate action information in the transition model
calibration_and_uncertainty: Prediction errors and across-subject summaries are reported; no formal reliability, coverage, calibration slope, or calibrated predictive interval
external_validation: No external cohort, clinical device, or independent simulator validation
decision_utility: Closed-loop simulated glucose control versus PID, including time in target ranges and CVGA outcomes.
safety_evaluation: Predicted-glucose rules suspend insulin below 70 mg/dL and add insulin above 180 mg/dL; hypoglycemia outcomes are reported in simulation only
statistical_analysis: Descriptive mean and variability across 10 virtual subjects and prediction-error summaries; no clearly reported inferential hypothesis test
causal_language: The article motivates safe control but does not make an identified causal treatment-effect claim
estimand: NA: no causal estimand; objective is closed-loop glycemic control
confounding_strategy: NA: simulator policy experiment rather than observational causal estimation
positivity_and_overlap: NA: no treatment-overlap estimand; explored insulin support is not formally characterized
counterfactual_validation: No real-patient counterfactual validation; only virtual-subject closed-loop behavior
code_access: NI: no public paper-specific source-code repository identified in the full text
weights_access: NI: trained model weights are not reported as publicly available
data_access: Simulator-generated data are not released; UVA/Padova simulator access is separately governed
preprocessing_reproducibility: The 5-minute sampling, 60-minute history, feature construction, model architecture, reward, and safety rules are described; reusable preprocessing artifacts are NI
randomness: Stochastic RL and virtual meals are used; random seeds and a complete seed protocol are NI
evidence_anchors: Official IEEE Access article, DOI 10.1109/ACCESS.2021.3100007: Methods Sec. III and Algorithms 1-3; Experiments Sec. IV, Tables 1-4, Figs. 3-7; Appendices A-B.
appraisal_strengths: Clear action-conditioned transition model, long closed-loop simulator evaluation, clinically interpretable glucose outcomes, and explicit safety overrides
appraisal_limitations: Simulation-only evidence in the same virtual populations; no independent validation, calibrated uncertainty, or horizon-resolved rollout-fidelity analysis
source_status: Full official IEEE version-of-record PDF inspected

title: A data-driven Alzheimer's disease progression simulator for retrospective validation and prospective Phase III power design.
domain: Alzheimer disease progression and anti-amyloid Phase III trial simulation
dataset_or_cohort: ADNI amyloid-positive longitudinal cohort plus published aggregate results from six anti-amyloid randomized trials.
sample_scale: 351 ADNI participants with 1,256 visits; 100 simulations of 150 subjects per arm for centiloid analyses and 500 virtual trials per power design across 50-800 subjects per arm
institution_count: ADNI is multisite and six external trials are represented; exact institution count is NI
split_strategy: Natural-history dynamics are learned from ADNI; trial-specific amyloid-clearance calibration and leave-one-trial-out effect/variance calibration use published trial aggregates, so external comparisons are not fully frozen
observation_process: Irregular longitudinal amyloid PET, tau PET, MRI atrophy, and clinical measures; simulated trial visits every 3 months.
missingness: Missing biomarker observations are excluded from the likelihood rather than globally imputed
censoring_or_competing_events: Trial dropout, death, and competing events are NI and are not explicitly simulated
state: Latent disease state learned from amyloid, tau, MRI-derived atrophy, and clinical modalities, with trial-specific baseline latent initialization.
observation_decoder: Variational-autoencoder decoders map latent trajectories back to observed biomarkers and cognition
action: Anti-amyloid intervention represented as a piecewise modification of amyloid-clearance dynamics; placebo is the no-intervention comparator.
action_provenance: Simulated treatment profiles calibrated to published aggregate amyloid reductions from six RCTs.
transition_mechanism: Masked amyloid-cascade neural ODE in latent space with VAE observation models.
maximum_horizon: 18 months for four trial emulations and 27 months for gantenerumab, with results at multiple intermediate visits
rollout_regime: Free-running latent ODE trajectories for placebo and treated arms, repeated 500 times per trial design.
capability_claim: Counterfactual — compares simulated placebo and alternative anti-amyloid interventions and estimates treatment effects/power.
baselines: Linear mixed-effects, ridge regression, gradient boosting, observed placebo arms, and alternative calibration settings
state_fidelity_metrics: Multimodal reconstruction/trajectory comparisons and aggregate clinical endpoint agreement with published trials; exact metrics vary by modality and trial.
transition_metrics: Longitudinal trajectories and treatment-effect estimates at repeated visits through 18 or 27 months.
rollout_stability: Power curves and endpoint agreement are reported by trial duration/sample size; repeated simulations assess Monte Carlo stability
action_sensitivity: Six drug-specific clearance profiles and alternative treatment scenarios; treatment magnitude/timing are explicitly encoded, though calibrated from target-drug aggregate data.
calibration_and_uncertainty: Repeated virtual trials provide empirical variability and power; no reliability diagram, interval coverage, calibration slope, or equivalent formal predictive calibration
external_validation: Aggregate retrospective comparison with six RCTs; not fully frozen because baseline state and amyloid kinetics are trial-specific and calibrated to published trial information.
decision_utility: Prospective power and sample-size design for Phase III trials, compared with statistical and machine-learning simulators.
safety_evaluation: NI/negative: adverse events such as ARIA, treatment discontinuation, and treatment-related hazard are not modeled
statistical_analysis: Five-fold predictive-baseline cross-validation; 100 replicated 150-per-arm centiloid simulations; 500 virtual trials per power design with 50-800 subjects per arm
causal_language: Uses causal-intervention and counterfactual terminology for amyloid lowering and downstream outcomes
estimand: Treated-minus-placebo biomarker or CDR-SB endpoint difference and the resulting empirical power at specified trial horizons
confounding_strategy: No individual-level treatment-confounding adjustment; ADNI supplies natural-history dynamics and trial aggregate changes calibrate intervention effects
positivity_and_overlap: No propensity, overlap, or support diagnostic for treatment response is reported
counterfactual_validation: Retrospective reproduction of published trial-level trajectories/endpoints provides partial validation, not individual counterfactual truth
code_access: Partial/public — training code is inspectable at the paper-reported Inria GitLab; trial-simulation code is stated as planned upon acceptance.
weights_access: NI: pretrained model weights or a fixed model checkpoint are not clearly reported as public
data_access: Credentialed — ADNI data require application; published RCT aggregates are publicly reported.
preprocessing_reproducibility: Partial — cohort criteria, modalities, equations, and pseudocode are detailed, but the full trial pipeline and fitted parameters are not yet released.
randomness: Monte Carlo repetitions are explicit; complete random-seed values and deterministic environment details are NI
evidence_anchors: medRxiv v1 full text, DOI 10.64898/2026.05.03.26352317: Results, Tables 1-2 and Figs. 1-5; Methods sections on ADNI cohort, latent ODE dynamics, intervention calibration, virtual trials, and power.
appraisal_strengths: Multiple trial targets, multimodal latent dynamics, horizon-specific outcomes, repeated power simulations, and inspectable public code
appraisal_limitations: Preprint; trial-specific adaptation, no full causal identification or support analysis, no safety modeling, and incomplete release of trial code/weights.
source_status: Full medRxiv v1 preprint PDF inspected

observation_process: Longitudinal estimated glomerular filtration rate with age, genotype, variant, and clinical covariates at registry visits
missingness: NI: longitudinal missingness handling for the source registry is not fully restated; synthetic generation preserves specified marginal distributions and correlations
censoring_or_competing_events: Kidney-failure censoring, death, transplantation, and other competing events are not explicitly modeled in the reported trial scenarios
state: Age, baseline eGFR, causal gene/variant, relevant covariates, individual random effects, and disease-model parameters
observation_decoder: Direct model output is longitudinal eGFR and derived eGFR slope or endpoint
action: Hypothetical percentage changes to disease-progression parameters DPT50, gamma1, or gamma2; placebo leaves parameters unchanged
action_provenance: User-specified assumed treatment effects, not observed clinical interventions
transition_mechanism: Genotype-specific nonlinear mixed-effects eGFR progression models combined with conditional-inference-tree generation of synthetic trial populations
maximum_horizon: Quarterly virtual-trial follow-up from 0.75 to 3 years
rollout_regime: One hundred replicated placebo-versus-treatment virtual trials across effect sizes, durations, and cohort definitions
capability_claim: Counterfactual: assumed treatment modifications are compared with placebo to estimate endpoint behavior and power
baselines: Placebo, alternative disease-model parameter targets, durations, sample sizes, and analysis endpoints
state_fidelity_metrics: Synthetic-cohort distributions and correlations are checked against source high-risk samples
transition_metrics: Prior disease-model test-set and visual-predictive-check evidence is cited; current case reports emphasize eGFR trajectories, slopes, and endpoint power
rollout_stability: Power estimates and 95% intervals are reported across 100 simulation replicates and multiple trial durations
action_sensitivity: Structured perturbations vary treatment target, percentage effect, duration, cohort, and analysis strategy
calibration_and_uncertainty: Interindividual variability and 100-replicate power uncertainty with approximate 95% confidence intervals are included; no formal predictive calibration
external_validation: Prior independent test evidence for the natural-history model is referenced, but no independent clinical validation of simulated treatment response is provided
decision_utility: The Shiny simulator estimates sample size, duration, analysis choice, and power for rare-disease trial design
safety_evaluation: NI/negative: no adverse-event, treatment-toxicity, or safety-hazard process is modeled
statistical_analysis: Repeated simulations, power calculations, confidence intervals based on simulation standard error, and mixed-model endpoint analyses
causal_language: Treatment effects are explicitly hypothetical model parameter changes; causal interpretation is assumption-based
estimand: Between-arm difference in eGFR slope or end-of-trial eGFR and the associated rejection probability/power
confounding_strategy: NA for simulated randomized allocation; source natural-history confounding is not used to estimate observed treatment effects
positivity_and_overlap: NA/NI: simulated arms have designed support, but no empirical treatment-overlap diagnostic exists
counterfactual_validation: No observed treated cohort or patient-level counterfactual outcome validates the assumed response
code_access: Partial: a public R Shiny application and selected Data S1 code snippets are available; a complete inspectable source repository is NI
weights_access: NA for neural weights; model parameter information is described, but a complete fitted-object release is NI
data_access: Registry data are not public; synthetic trial cohorts can be generated through the application
preprocessing_reproducibility: Model equations, synthetic-population workflow, parameter perturbations, and trial settings are documented; exact end-to-end source-data preparation is not public
randomness: Random effects and 100 simulation replicates are specified; random seeds are NI
evidence_anchors: Clinical and Translational Science full text, DOI 10.1002/psp4.70258: Methods on CTS development and simulation; case-report Results and figures/tables; Discussion limitations; Data S1 code examples.
appraisal_strengths: Directly decision-oriented rare-disease simulations, explicit scenario perturbations, repeated trials, and an accessible interactive implementation
appraisal_limitations: Small high-risk source subsets, single-registry provenance, hypothetical treatment response, no safety model, and no independent intervention validation
source_status: Full open-access journal text and available supplements inspected through Europe PMC

title: Control of Magnetic Surgical Robots With Model-Based Simulators and Reinforcement Learning.
domain: Magnetic surgical robotics; model-based reinforcement learning
dataset_or_cohort: Physical MagnetoSuture benchtop platform with a 22-gauge needle, four electromagnetic coils, and camera tracking.
sample_scale: 34,742 physical transitions collected in approximately 3.2 hours; downstream simulated training up to 2.5 million steps.
institution_count: One laboratory hardware system; no tissue, animal, patient, or multi-institution sample
split_strategy: Validation and test losses are reported, but exact split proportions and temporal grouping are NI
observation_process: Camera-derived planar needle position and heading after discrete current pulses (100 ms actuation plus 200 ms rest, approximately 3 Hz).
missingness: NA: complete engineered sensor transitions are used; no missing-observation process is reported
censoring_or_competing_events: NA: no clinical censoring or competing event; hardware episodes reset when the robot leaves the valid workspace
observation_decoder: Fully connected neural network directly predicts the next planar pose
action_provenance: Manual exploration commands for data collection; learned TD3 commands for simulated training and physical deployment.
transition_mechanism: Deterministic neural one-step model used as a model-based simulator for TD3 policy learning.
maximum_horizon: One-step held-out transition evaluation; learned-simulator episodes usually span 5-30 steps; policy training uses 500,000-2.5 million simulator steps
rollout_regime: Free-running simulator during policy training and real closed-loop transfer to the physical device.
capability_claim: Planning — policy selects sequential coil commands using learned-model rollouts.
baselines: Physics-based simulator, pure off-policy learning, and task/controller variants
state_fidelity_metrics: Real-robot root-mean-square position error for center, random-target, and square-path tasks
transition_metrics: Learned next-state model validation loss 0.033 and test loss 0.045; no direct multi-step trajectory-fidelity metric
rollout_stability: Successful multi-step physical trajectories are shown, but transition/control error is not reported as a function of the 5-30-step rollout horizon
action_sensitivity: No formal action-removal or structured command-perturbation evaluation; several target/path tasks test policy behavior
calibration_and_uncertainty: NI/negative: no predictive intervals, ensemble uncertainty, reliability analysis, or formal calibration
external_validation: Simulator-trained policies transfer to the same laboratory MagnetoSuture apparatus; this is sim-to-real evidence but not an independent site, device family, or frozen external cohort
decision_utility: Real-hardware RMS error is approximately 5.3-7.4 mm for model-based agents versus about 31 mm for the pure-physics-simulator agent on reported tasks
safety_evaluation: Coil overheating/cooling, magnetic dead zones, zero-current avoidance, workspace resets, and supervision are described; no biological safety or formal hazard stress test
statistical_analysis: Training summaries include means with two-standard-deviation bands across repeated agents, but agent count, seeds, and inferential tests are not consistently specified
causal_language: NA: control performance is not framed as an identified causal treatment effect
confounding_strategy: NA: engineered control experiment, not observational treatment-effect estimation
positivity_and_overlap: No formal action-support diagnostic; physical data collection explores the allowed command space
counterfactual_validation: NA: sim-to-real control validation is not patient counterfactual validation
code_access: NI: no public paper-specific code repository identified
weights_access: NI: no trained network weights identified as public
data_access: NI: the 34,742-transition physical dataset is not reported as publicly downloadable
preprocessing_reproducibility: Partial — hardware, state extraction, normalization, architecture, and training are described, but executable preprocessing is absent.
randomness: Random targets and repeated agent training are used; complete seeds and run count are NI
evidence_anchors: IEEE TMRB full text, DOI 10.1109/TMRB.2022.3214426: Secs. II-B-II-D on data, model, and TD3; Sec. III and Figs. 4-7 on model loss and real-robot transfer; hardware safety descriptions.
appraisal_strengths: Direct learned-transition validation plus frozen sim-to-real closed-loop evaluation and concrete hardware hazard controls
appraisal_limitations: Single apparatus, one-step simulator metric only, no uncertainty/action ablation, limited safety scope, and no public artifacts.
source_status: Full peer-reviewed article inspected through PMC/Europe PMC

title: Development of a model-based clinical trial simulation platform to optimize the design of clinical trials for Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
domain: Duchenne muscular dystrophy natural history and clinical trial simulation
dataset_or_cohort: Duchenne Regulatory Science Consortium database: 15 clinical studies comprising trials and natural-history cohorts.
sample_scale: 15 studies with 1,505 participants and 27,252 observations; development uses 11 primarily North American studies (1,141 participants; 19,996 observations), with four non-US studies (364 participants; 7,256 observations) held out
institution_count: Multiple international studies and sites; exact unique institution count is NI
split_strategy: Eleven primarily North American studies form the development set; four non-US studies are reserved for external visual predictive checks
observation_process: Irregular longitudinal clinical outcomes from age 4 through advanced disease: NSAA, FVC, and climb/stand/walk-run velocities.
missingness: Missing functional-test values are handled through the model-specific M4 censoring convention; no general-purpose imputation scheme is reported
censoring_or_competing_events: Loss of measurable function is represented through M4 censoring; death and dropout are not modeled as competing events
state: Age, baseline functional score, race, steroid use, mutation class, study type, and individual random effects.
observation_decoder: Nonlinear mixed-effects model directly produces each clinical outcome trajectory
action: User-defined hypothetical treatment timing and magnitude applied to progression-model parameters to create active arms.
action_provenance: Simulated treatment effects; not estimated from observed treatment response in the platform evaluation.
transition_mechanism: Product of Chapman–Richards growth and sigmoid Imax decline functions with fixed/random effects and residual error.
maximum_horizon: Age-spanning natural-history trajectories and user-defined trial durations; external VPCs cover observed longitudinal follow-up.
rollout_regime: Free-running parametric trajectory simulation, virtual trials, and visual predictive checks with 500 simulated datasets.
capability_claim: Counterfactual — placebo/historical-control versus hypothetical active treatment trial simulation.
baselines: Natural-history/placebo model and alternative covariate/model forms; no action-agnostic machine-learning comparator
state_fidelity_metrics: Goodness-of-fit plots and visual predictive checks for five endpoints with observed percentiles versus simulated prediction intervals.
transition_metrics: Age-resolved longitudinal VPCs in development and external cohorts; no single aggregate transition metric.
rollout_stability: Internal and external trajectory distributions are assessed over age; explicit degradation by increasing simulated trial horizon is NI
action_sensitivity: Treatment-effect size, timing, and affected parameter can be varied in the CTS platform.
calibration_and_uncertainty: Interindividual random effects and visual predictive intervals quantify variability; no formal forecast reliability or interval-coverage calibration is reported
external_validation: Frozen evaluation on four non-US studies held out from model development.
decision_utility: Trial-design platform for endpoint, enrichment, duration, placebo/historical-control, and treatment-effect scenarios; no prospective decision-impact study.
safety_evaluation: NI/negative: treatment toxicity, adverse events, and safety hazards are not represented
statistical_analysis: Likelihood-based nonlinear mixed-effects modeling, covariate testing, goodness-of-fit, and visual predictive checks with prediction intervals
causal_language: Uses hypothetical treatment-effect and trial-simulation language; it does not identify a causal effect from observed treatment assignment
estimand: NI: no explicit causal treatment estimand is mathematically defined in the article
confounding_strategy: Covariates explain natural-history heterogeneity; no treatment-confounding strategy is needed for hypothetical randomized arms and none estimates a clinical treatment effect
positivity_and_overlap: NI/NA: no empirical treatment-overlap assessment; virtual active/placebo support is imposed by design
counterfactual_validation: No observed active-treatment cohort validates the hypothetical response; external validation concerns untreated disease trajectories
code_access: Public/partial — NONMEM model codes are provided in the article supplement.
weights_access: NA for neural weights; parameter estimates and model specification are available in article/supplement materials
data_access: Underlying consortium and trial data are governed and not publicly downloadable
preprocessing_reproducibility: Partial — CDISC harmonization, endpoint definitions, model equations, and code are described, but source data are restricted.
randomness: Virtual patients sample interindividual variability; visual-predictive simulations are stochastic; exact seed protocol is NI
evidence_anchors: Clinical and Translational Science full text, DOI 10.1002/psp4.12753: cohort/model-development Methods; internal and external VPC Results; trial-simulation platform description; Appendix S5 model code.
appraisal_strengths: Large integrated longitudinal dataset, true geographically external validation, multiple clinically meaningful outcomes, and accessible model code
appraisal_limitations: Treatment effects are hypothetical, dropout and safety are not modeled, governed data limit reproduction, and clinical decision impact is untested.
source_status: Full open-access journal text and Appendix S5 inspected through Europe PMC

title: Generating whole-brain neural activity and behavior through unified latent dynamics
domain: Whole-brain neural dynamics and behavior in C. elegans
dataset_or_cohort: Single immobilized C. elegans whole-brain calcium-imaging and behavior recording used by NEBULA
sample_scale: One recording with 109 neurons over 1,080 seconds; no independent worm or session
institution_count: One previously published experimental recording; institution count is effectively one source laboratory
split_strategy: No held-out subject/session or external dataset; generated and perturbation results are evaluated against the same recording and its distributions
observation_process: Whole-brain calcium activity and manually/algorithmically assigned fictive behavior sampled as a continuous time series; downstream body motion is heuristic/simulated.
missingness: NI: no conventional missing-data mechanism is described for the selected recording
censoring_or_competing_events: NA: no censoring, mortality, or competing clinical event
state: Three-dimensional latent state inferred from neural causal history.
observation_decoder: GRU neural decoder predicts continuous neural activity and GRU behavioral decoder outputs categorical state logits
action: Latent noise injection and state-steering intervention; no observed biological action or treatment variable in the base model.
action_provenance: Purely simulated latent interventions selected by investigators.
transition_mechanism: Stochastic Gaussian Markov transition in latent space with neural and behavioral recurrent decoders.
maximum_horizon: 30,000-step autonomous rollout (about 168 minutes); 1,000 repeated 60-second rollouts; 10,000-step steering simulations
rollout_regime: Autonomous free-running stochastic latent dynamics with repeated generated trajectories and simulated steering.
capability_claim: Counterfactual — paper explicitly presents latent interventions/steering as counterfactual manipulation of neural-behavior dynamics.
baselines: Empirical behavior/neural distributions, unsteered rollout, noise perturbations, and architectural analyses; no independent state-of-the-art forecasting baseline is central
state_fidelity_metrics: Behavior-state frequencies, functional-connectivity reconstruction, kinematic dispersal, and manifold fidelity
transition_metrics: Behavior transition-matrix correlations/divergences and generated trajectory statistics; evaluated on same-session distributions.
rollout_stability: 30,000-step generation, 1,000 rollouts to 60 seconds, and robustness across intervention-noise intensities.
action_sensitivity: Unsteered baseline versus latent noise/desired-state steering at varied intensities; interventions are not validated against biological perturbations.
calibration_and_uncertainty: Stochastic variance and repeated rollouts are reported; no predictive calibration or interval coverage.
external_validation: No held-out animal, independent recording, freely moving worm, or biological intervention validation
decision_utility: The model demonstrates simulated steering and hypothesis-generation value, not a clinical or experimental decision-impact study
safety_evaluation: Robustness and failure behavior under global and localized latent-noise perturbations are examined; no biological or clinical hazard test
statistical_analysis: KL divergence, chi-square tests, R-squared connectivity comparisons, repeated stochastic rollouts, and perturbation-error maps
causal_language: Uses digital-twin and counterfactual-intervention language, but does not establish biological causal identification
estimand: NI: no explicit causal estimand for a real intervention
confounding_strategy: No adjustment for observational or experimental confounding in the single-recording analysis
positivity_and_overlap: NA/NI: simulated steering support is defined in latent space; biological intervention positivity is not assessed
counterfactual_validation: No optogenetic, neural-ablation, or other real perturbation validates the predicted counterfactual response
code_access: NI: no inspectable paper implementation repository identified
weights_access: NI: fitted model weights are not publicly released
data_access: Public source neural/behavior recording is linked through the cited OSF dataset
preprocessing_reproducibility: Architecture and transformation steps are described, but exact executable preprocessing, fitted parameters, and code are NI
randomness: One thousand stochastic rollouts and 20 samples per perturbation intensity are described; seed values are NI
evidence_anchors: bioRxiv v2 full text, DOI 10.64898/2026.06.05.730482: Results Secs. 2.2-2.5 and Figs. 2-4; Methods Secs. 4.1-4.5; supplementary robustness and intervention analyses.
appraisal_strengths: Unusually long free generation, multimodal decoding, explicit stochastic modeling, repeated perturbations, and quantitative aggregate-dynamics checks
appraisal_limitations: Single training/evaluation recording, no held-out subject/session, no biological perturbation validation, no calibration, and no code/weights.
source_status: Full bioRxiv v2 preprint PDF inspected

title: Machine Learning for Mechanical Ventilation Control

institution_count: One experimental bench/laboratory; no patient, animal, or multicenter cohort
split_strategy: A separate learned simulator is fit per lung setting; open-loop test trajectories are used, but exact train/validation/test proportions and grouping are NI
observation_process: High-frequency airway pressure and valve-control histories during approximately 9-second, 300-step breaths; six R/C lung settings.
missingness: NA: engineered sensor streams are treated as complete; missing pressure/control handling is not reported
censoring_or_competing_events: NA: no patient censoring or competing event; breaths can terminate through safety overrides
state: Recent pressure history and control history, with lung resistance/compliance setting implicit through separate models.
observation_decoder: Boundary-specific and general deep regression models predict the next pressure and are stitched into a simulator
action: Continuous inspiratory valve command; expiratory control is hard-coded.

transition_mechanism: Autoregressive neural pressure simulator; PID-residual neural controller and RL baselines trained using model rollouts.

rollout_regime: Recursive free-running pressure simulation and real closed-loop hardware control.

baselines: Physics-based models, exhaustive grid-searched PID, direct learned controller variants, and residual-PID ablations
state_fidelity_metrics: L1 waveform-tracking error across six ISO pressure targets and six lung settings
transition_metrics: Open-loop error plotted by recursive prediction step to 25 steps (Fig. 5).
rollout_stability: Closed-loop pressure tracking over full breaths and multiple target waveforms/settings; hardware safety aborts constrain failures.

statistical_analysis: Averaged L1 scores over inspiratory phases and six waveforms, simulator horizon curves, and controller ablations; inferential tests and run-level confidence intervals are NI
causal_language: NA: engineered control performance is not an identified causal treatment effect
confounding_strategy: NA: physical control experiment rather than observational treatment assignment
positivity_and_overlap: Exploration is constrained to a safe pressure region; no formal support/coverage diagnostic is reported
counterfactual_validation: NA: sim-to-real bench transfer is not a patient counterfactual validation
code_access: Unavailable for the reported learned simulator/controller; the underlying PVP ventilator platform is open source.
weights_access: NI: trained simulator and controller weights are not reported as public
data_access: Unavailable — collected pressure/control trajectories were not released.
preprocessing_reproducibility: Partial — hardware, signals, history windows, architectures, and training procedures are described; exact data volume and executable pipeline are absent.
randomness: Exploration and neural optimization are stochastic; exact random seeds and repeated-run protocol are NI
evidence_anchors: Author arXiv v4 full text, arXiv:2102.06779: Methods Secs. 3-5 and Figs. 3-9; Sec. 4.1/Fig. 5 recursive prediction; Appendix B and Tables 3-5.
appraisal_strengths: True horizon-resolved simulator evaluation, explicit sim-to-real closed-loop testing, robust multi-setting controller, and concrete hardware safety interlocks
appraisal_limitations: Benchtop rather than patient validation, same-platform transfer, no uncertainty/calibration, incomplete dataset reporting, and no released learned artifacts.

title: OMG-RL:Offline Model-based Guided Reward Learning for Heparin Treatment
publication_status: Peer-reviewed journal article (Biomedical Engineering Advances, 2025); extraction checked against the matching author arXiv v2 manuscript
domain: ICU heparin dosing; offline model-based reinforcement learning
dataset_or_cohort: MIMIC-III adult ICU records for patients receiving intravenous heparin
institution_count: One source hospital/database, Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center MIMIC-III
split_strategy: Random 80/20 patient-level split within MIMIC-III; no independent database or site validation
observation_process: Hourly records from 7 to 72 hours after heparin initiation, using laboratory values, vital signs, scores, and outcomes
missingness: High-missing-rate features are removed; derived scores are reconstructed; sample-and-hold, KNN, and linear imputation are applied; outliers are removed and values normalized
censoring_or_competing_events: Trajectories shorter than 7 hours are excluded and follow-up is capped at 72 hours; discharge, death, bleeding, and other competing events are not modeled
state: Sixteen preprocessed clinical variables; aPTT and heparin dose are excluded from the state vector
observation_decoder: Four-layer fully connected probabilistic ensemble predicts next state and reward
action: Intravenous heparin dose discretized into six quantile-based action classes
action_provenance: Observed clinician-administered doses in the offline data and learned policy actions during model rollouts
transition_mechanism: Ensemble probabilistic dynamics model with recursive rollout, conservative model-based Q-learning, and guided reward learning
rollout_regime: Free-running model rollouts for policy training/evaluation plus offline weighted-importance-sampling evaluation on held-out patients.
capability_claim: Planning — optimizes a sequential heparin dosing policy through learned-model rollouts.
baselines: COMBO, SAC, BCQ, Double DQN, Dueling DQN, DQN, model-free/model-based variants, and clinician behavior
state_fidelity_metrics: Policy-return, WIS, action-agreement, PT/INR dose-tendency, and simulated treatment-success summaries
transition_metrics: No direct held-out next-state RMSE, likelihood, calibration, or clinical-variable trajectory error is reported; return/Q-value behavior is used as indirect model evidence
rollout_stability: Only a 36-hour rollout setting is evaluated for treatment success; no degradation curve across model horizons is reported
action_sensitivity: Dose-action distributions and clinician agreement are shown, but no action-removal, action-shuffle, or controlled dose perturbation validates response sensitivity
calibration_and_uncertainty: Ensemble variance/conservatism is used as a model-error proxy; formal calibration and interval coverage are NI
external_validation: No external hospital, temporal cohort, prospective deployment, or frozen clinical validation
decision_utility: Offline policy value via weighted importance sampling and simulated 36-hour therapeutic-success episodes; no prospective or clinician-in-the-loop evaluation
safety_evaluation: aPTT therapeutic range is a limited safety proxy; bleeding, thrombosis, overdose severity, contraindications, and override/failure tests are NI
statistical_analysis: COMBO and OMG-RL use 500 episodes; results summarize five or ten experiments; treatment success uses 380 episodes over ten runs
causal_language: The paper claims improved policy value relative to clinician/model baselines, but causal identification remains partial and relies on offline policy evaluation assumptions
estimand: Offline policy value/return under the learned dosing policy, estimated in part with weighted importance sampling
confounding_strategy: State conditioning and offline RL/OPE are used, but explicit adjustment for time-varying treatment confounding is NI
positivity_and_overlap: No propensity/behavior-policy support or overlap diagnostic is reported despite offline policy learning
counterfactual_validation: No prospective or observed patient counterfactual validation; success for learned policies is generated by the learned model
code_access: NI: no inspectable implementation repository identified
weights_access: NI: ensemble and policy weights are not publicly released
data_access: Credentialed public access: MIMIC-III requires data-use training and approval
preprocessing_reproducibility: Cohort, variables, time window, imputation, action bins, algorithms, and hyperparameters are described; executable code is NI
randomness: Seven-model ensemble, five selected models, and five/ten repeated experiments are reported; exact random seeds are NI
evidence_anchors: Author arXiv v2 manuscript matching DOI 10.1016/j.bea.2025.100198: Methods and Algorithms 1-2; experimental setup; Results Figs. 2-8; limitations.
appraisal_strengths: Explicit held-out split, detailed missing-data pipeline, probabilistic ensemble, broad offline-RL baselines, WIS, and repeated simulations
appraisal_limitations: Same-source held-out evaluation, no direct transition-fidelity metric, no horizon drift analysis, limited safety proxy, and no complete causal-identification analysis
source_status: Publisher metadata verified; full extraction used the matching author arXiv v2 because the version-of-record PDF was not directly retrievable

title: SimulAD: a dynamical model for personalized simulation and disease staging in Alzheimer's disease.
domain: Alzheimer disease staging and personalized progression forecasting
dataset_or_cohort: ADNI development cohort and independent Geneva Memory Center (GMC) clinical cohort.
sample_scale: 442 ADNI participants and 93 GMC participants; 50 GMC participants had tau PET; GMC follow-up included 201 MMSE assessments across groups.
institution_count: ADNI is multisite and Geneva is one independent clinical center; exact ADNI site count is NI
split_strategy: The ADNI-fitted model is applied to GMC, but GMC-specific KNN imputation, FDG mapping, tracer correction, and a separately fitted GMC progression trajectory mean the external analysis is not frozen
observation_process: Irregular longitudinal clinical scores and MRI/amyloid-PET/FDG-PET in ADNI; GMC has baseline multimodal imaging and longitudinal MMSE only.
missingness: Substantial modality missingness is addressed through defined imputation/harmonization procedures and sensitivity analyses; exact missing proportions vary by modality
censoring_or_competing_events: Conversion status is analyzed, but death, dropout, and competing-risk censoring are not modeled as dynamic events
state: Four biomarker z-scores: clinical, gray-matter atrophy, amyloid, and glucose metabolism; disease severity is position on the reference trajectory.
observation_decoder: Dynamical model maps disease time to observed biomarker and cognitive trajectories
action: No action evaluated in this study; the paper cites prior capability to simulate anti-amyloid treatment effects.
action_provenance: NA for current experiments; referenced anti-amyloid action is a simulated intervention from prior work.
transition_mechanism: Coupled ordinary differential equations governing the four biomarker z-scores.
maximum_horizon: Personalized GMC evolution simulated for five years; ADNI/GMC reference trajectories span long-term disease time.
rollout_regime: Free-running forward/backward ODE trajectories and five-year individual prediction.
capability_claim: Passive forecasting/disease staging in the present experiments; the paper additionally repeats a counterfactual anti-amyloid capability claim from prior work.
baselines: Observed follow-up, population-level biomarker relationships, disease-stage groups, and simpler association analyses; no prominent action/model-free baseline applies
state_fidelity_metrics: Group separation by estimated stage, cross-modal correlations, converter/nonconverter associations, and biomarker agreement
transition_metrics: ADNI-versus-GMC trajectory errors (6%–9% for z-scores; 3%–12% for decoded modalities) and GMC MMSE absolute error 1.8–2.4 points over follow-up.
rollout_stability: Prediction is evaluated at multiple future times through five years; uncertainty growth by horizon is not formally calibrated
action_sensitivity: NA: no action variable or intervention perturbation in the evaluated study
calibration_and_uncertainty: Error distributions and preprocessing sensitivity checks are reported; no calibrated predictive intervals, reliability diagram, or coverage analysis
external_validation: Independent GMC cohort with different acquisition protocols, with material GMC-specific adaptation and trajectory fitting
decision_utility: Potential utility is individualized disease staging, prognosis, and trial enrichment; no prospective clinical decision-impact study is performed
statistical_analysis: Group comparisons, correlations, trajectory-error summaries, and sensitivity analyses are reported; exact test details appear with results/figures
causal_language: Disease-progression language is mechanistic, but this article does not estimate a causal treatment effect
confounding_strategy: NA for treatment causality; demographic/measurement differences are handled through preprocessing and sensitivity analyses rather than causal adjustment
positivity_and_overlap: NA: no treatment assignment or action support
counterfactual_validation: NA: no intervention counterfactual is evaluated in this article
code_access: Unavailable — the article calls SimulAD research software and provides no inspectable repository.
weights_access: NI: fitted model weights/parameters are not released as a reusable artifact
data_access: ADNI is credentialed; GMC data availability is request/institution-governed and not openly released.
preprocessing_reproducibility: Partial — imaging pipelines, KNN imputation, FDG estimation, and tracer correction are described, but complete code/data are unavailable.
randomness: Predominantly deterministic fitting/simulation; random initialization or seeds are NI
evidence_anchors: Author-hosted final article PDF, DOI 10.1016/j.neurobiolaging.2021.12.015: Methods Secs. 2.1-2.6 and Tables 1-2; Results Figs. 3-6 and Table 4; Discussion/Conclusion.
appraisal_strengths: Independent clinical-cohort application, multimodal state evaluation, personalized long-horizon trajectories, and explicit sensitivity analysis
appraisal_limitations: External cohort is adapted rather than fully frozen, no standard forecast baseline or horizon degradation, no calibration/public code, and treatment counterfactual capability is not tested here.
source_status: Full author-hosted final article PDF inspected

title: The Coupled Stochastic Dynamical System: A Generative Model for Simulating and Forecasting Youth Mental Health Trajectories
domain: Youth mental health; multimodal longitudinal simulation and forecasting
dataset_or_cohort: GLOBEM multi-year cohort with passive sensing, ecological momentary assessment, and survey outcomes
sample_scale: 496 GLOBEM participants across four clusters; detailed participant-level decoding/forecasting uses the 50 centroid-nearest participants per cluster (200 total)
institution_count: Multi-year cohort with university/student recruitment; exact unique institution count is NI
split_strategy: Causal rolling-origin forecasts with future observations withheld; split-half target-corridor analysis checks leakage/stability, but there is no independent cohort or strict end-to-end prospective split
observation_process: Sub-hourly behavioral and physiological streams, day-level burdens, EMA observations, and periodic surveys with channel-specific timing
missingness: Finite observations and channel support are used, with preprocessing/imputation details in supplementary sections S7/S11; missingness is not modeled as an informative observation process
censoring_or_competing_events: Attrition, clinical escalation, hospitalization, and competing events are not explicitly modeled in the reported forecasts
state: Coupled traits, daily burdens, sub-hourly behavior/physiology, latent mental-health regime, and observation-channel states
observation_decoder: Channel-specific stochastic emission models produce passive-sensing, EMA, and survey observations
action: Intervention processes are represented structurally, but no administered action is evaluated in the empirical batch
action_provenance: Hypothetical model intervention/counterfactual input; current validation uses natural observational trajectories
transition_mechanism: Coupled stochastic dynamical system with mechanistic dependencies, hidden-state transitions, emissions, and particle-based parameter/state inference
maximum_horizon: Forecasts at 1, 3, 7, 14, and 21 days; generative simulations are also used for occupancy, transition, and target-corridor analyses
rollout_regime: Accepted posterior particles seed repeated free-running trajectories; forecasts and distributional behavior are aggregated across simulations
capability_claim: Counterfactual: the architecture claims intervention simulation, although demonstrated empirical capability is passive forecasting
baselines: Persistence and prefix-mean forecasting nulls, hidden-state/transition summaries, and observed target corridors
state_fidelity_metrics: Cluster and individual target-corridor coverage, state occupancy, regime prevalence, and observed-versus-simulated summary distributions
transition_metrics: Transition-matrix/occupancy agreement, drift correlations, forecast R-squared, within-subject skill, and balanced accuracy across horizons
rollout_stability: Results are explicitly resolved at five horizons through 21 days and compared with nulls; long-horizon performance declines are visible
action_sensitivity: No administered-action, action-removal, action-shuffle, or intervention-parameter response experiment is reported
calibration_and_uncertainty: Compatible parameter ensembles, participant uncertainty corridors, 5,000 subject-block bootstrap intervals, and horizon-specific calibration plots with linear fits at 1 and 21 days
external_validation: No independent cohort, institution, or geographically external validation
decision_utility: Forecasting and early-warning capability could support monitoring, but no clinician decision, intervention selection, or prospective outcome improvement is tested
safety_evaluation: Low-burden structural targets for unmeasured mania/OCD/psychosis and a relaxed suicidality constraint are included; hazardous-transition calibration and clinical safety validation are absent
statistical_analysis: Five thousand subject-block bootstrap replicates, horizon-specific metrics, ANOVA/group comparisons, repeated particles/simulations, and calibration analyses
causal_language: Uses counterfactual and intervention-process language, but current data do not identify an intervention effect
estimand: NI: no explicit causal estimand for an intervention response
confounding_strategy: No time-varying confounding strategy or causal adjustment for observational exposures is reported
positivity_and_overlap: No treatment/action propensity, support, or overlap diagnostic is reported
counterfactual_validation: No real intervention or independent outcome validates model-generated counterfactual trajectories
code_access: Code is described as planned for the accepted manuscript but is not currently public
weights_access: NI: accepted particles/fitted parameters are not released as public weights
data_access: GLOBEM data are available by request/application rather than unrestricted download
preprocessing_reproducibility: The main text and extensive supplement specify channels, preprocessing, clustering, inference, simulation, and metrics; runnable artifacts are not public
randomness: Particle acceptance, 20 repeated simulations, and bootstrap resampling are specified; complete seed values are NI
evidence_anchors: medRxiv v1 full text, DOI 10.64898/2026.07.26.26358943: Methods Secs. 2.1-2.7; Results Tables 3-4 and Figs. 3-5; Discussion; Data availability.
appraisal_strengths: Broad multimodal generative specification, substantial repeated simulation, horizon-resolved forecasting, null comparisons, bootstrap uncertainty, and transparent limitations
appraisal_limitations: Counterfactual/intervention claims exceed the tested passive setting; no external cohort, no strict end-to-end temporal split, no public code, and no hazard validation
source_status: Full medRxiv v1 preprint PDF inspected
